elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim..." — express "defend" verb running to Customer and its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: "indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees)".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right". "Services" and "Deliverables" are both terms used in the Order Form definition.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "Vendor's breach of Applicable Law", using the defined term at Section 1.2.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "any unauthorized access to, or disclosure of, Customer Data caused by Vendor".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Limb (d): "Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct"; consistent with the Excluded Claims carve-out in Section 21.3 so the indemnity remains uncapped.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "Customer shall give Vendor written notice of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "Vendor shall control its defence and settlement" — control expressly allocated to the indemnifying party.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: "Customer's indemnification obligations under this Agreement are limited to third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law." The document contains no competing Customer indemnity to contradict this.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Same limb (a) IP indemnity satisfies the fallback core grant.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no modification exclusion was added, which is at least as favourable to Customer as the fallback contemplates, so the condition does not bind.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no combination exclusion inserted; absence is more favourable to Customer than the fallback allowance.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no specifications exclusion inserted; absence does not defeat the fallback.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph contains no procure/modify/replace remedy ladder; nothing in the rendered text creates the remedies Section 9.3 calls "the remedies required by Section 20.5".

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-on-failure mechanic appears anywhere in the inserted or retained language.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x annual Fees super-cap is stated; Section 21.3 instead treats indemnification obligations as uncapped Excluded Claims.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all ten preferred elements are delivered in one inserted paragraph (defend/indemnify/hold harmless for Customer and Affiliates; IP, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incident, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct limbs; notice, Vendor control of defence and settlement, reasonable cooperation; and an express cap on Customer's indemnity to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law).

Fallback is incomplete (no procure/modify/replace ladder, no refund fallback, no 3x annual Fees super-cap), but that is immaterial because the preferred level is fully met. The drafter's reasoning for skipping the super-cap is sound: Section 21.3 already lists indemnification obligations as uncapped Excluded Claims, so importing a 3x cap would be a downgrade.

Minimal: the insertion tracks the model language for a missing clause, adds no survival tail, no at-own-expense wording, no extra damages categories or procedures beyond the notice/control/cooperation mechanics the checklist requires, and no retained language was deleted or paraphrased.

Intent preserved: Section 9.3's termination trigger, Section 19.5's anti-disclaimer sentence, and Section 21.3's Excluded Claims all reference indemnification and now have an operative obligation to attach to; nothing in the insertion contradicts retained allocation, timing, or payment mechanics.

Two drafting hygiene points to verify before sending (neither defeats completeness): (i) confirm "Affiliates" is a defined term in the Agreement — it is not among the resolved definitions supplied; if it is undefined, use "its affiliates" in lower case or add the definition. (ii) Section 9.3 still cross-refers to "the remedies required by Section 20.5"; numbering the insertion as Section 20.1 leaves that pointer dangling. This defect pre-existed the redline and curing it with a procure/modify/replace ladder would exceed the preferred checklist, so either renumber the insertion so the cross-reference resolves or flag the stale reference to Vendor as a conforming-change item.
